decisions.reason: The camera is close to the core offer, still has a dedicated page, and carries sunk qualification costs and public commitment, so management will persist with it.
This modular multi-model camera line is heavily invested and central to the announced push toward flexible, compact sensors, so dropping it would contradict the firm's stated direction.
The situational awareness suite is publicly showcased in a growing field, and slow uptake can be blamed on long space procurement cycles, so management stays committed.
The LiDAR is less visibly promoted, but it is costly to space-qualify and central to the docking and small-satellite strategy, so the firm keeps it despite modest exposure.
The radiation-hard camera line launched only in 2024 with its own page and several models, so heavy recent investment and visible commitment make withdrawal very unlikely.
The asteroid camera is newly launched and tied to mission-specific development, so its sunk costs and the long timelines of deep-space missions favour keeping it despite low visibility.
